t: How to Change the Lesson Type in Thrive Apprentice
c:
In this article, you'll learn about the different lesson types available in Thrive Apprentice, how to change a lesson's type, and when to use each format for the best learning experience.

Available Lesson Types

Thrive Apprentice offers three lesson types, each designed for a different content delivery style:

  • Text — A written lesson built using the Thrive Architect editor. Use text lessons for detailed explanations, step-by-step tutorials, downloadable resources, or any content that benefits from a rich text format with images, buttons, and other visual elements.
  • Video — A lesson centered around an embedded video. Use video lessons for demonstrations, walkthroughs, lectures, or any content that's easier to teach visually. You can still add supporting text below the video.
  • Audio — A lesson built around an embedded audio file. Use audio lessons for podcasts, interviews, guided meditations, or any content where students can listen on the go without needing to watch a screen.

Tip: You're not locked into your initial choice. You can change a lesson's type at any time without losing the content you've already added. The existing content is preserved—only the lesson's primary media format changes.

How to Change a Lesson Type

Follow these steps to switch a lesson from one type to another:

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Courses in the left sidebar and select the course that contains the lesson you want to modify.
  3. Open the Content tab to see all modules, chapters, and lessons.
  4. Hover over the lesson you want to change.
  5. Click Edit Details from the options that appear.
  6. In the lesson details panel, locate the Lesson Type setting.
  7. Select the new type: Text, Video, or Audio.
  8. If you selected Video or Audio, add the media source (e.g., a YouTube URL, Vimeo link, or uploaded file).
  9. Click Save to apply the change.

The lesson will now display in the new format when students access it.

When to Use Each Lesson Type

Choosing the right lesson type depends on your content and your audience's learning preferences. Here's a quick guide:

Text Lessons

Best for:

  • Detailed, reference-heavy content that students may want to search or skim.
  • Step-by-step instructions with screenshots or diagrams.
  • Lessons that include downloadable files, code snippets, or formatted tables.
  • Content that needs frequent updates—text is the easiest format to edit.

Video Lessons

Best for:

  • Visual demonstrations such as software tutorials or physical processes.
  • Lecture-style teaching where seeing the instructor builds connection.
  • Complex concepts that are easier to explain with animations or screen recordings.
  • Courses where engagement and completion rates are a priority—video tends to hold attention longer.

Audio Lessons

Best for:

  • Conversational content like interviews, discussions, or Q&A sessions.
  • Material that students can consume while multitasking—commuting, exercising, or doing chores.
  • Guided exercises such as meditations, language practice, or pronunciation drills.
  • Supplementary content that complements a primary video or text lesson.

Note: You can mix lesson types within the same course. A well-structured course often combines all three formats to cater to different learning styles and keep students engaged.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully learned how to change a lesson's type in Thrive Apprentice and when to use each format. Experiment with different lesson types to find the mix that works best for your content and your students.

t: How to Organize Lessons in Chapters
c:
In this article, you'll learn what chapters are in Thrive Apprentice, how they differ from modules, how to create and manage chapters, and best practices for structuring your course content so students can navigate it easily.

What Are Chapters?

Chapters are organizational containers within a Thrive Apprentice course that group related lessons together. They help you structure your content clearly so learners can navigate and progress through your course more smoothly. Think of chapters as sections within a book—each one covers a specific topic or theme and contains the individual lessons that teach that topic.

Chapters vs. Modules

Thrive Apprentice supports a hierarchical course structure with two levels of organization:

  • Modules — The top-level organizational unit. A module represents a major section or phase of your course. For example, in a photography course, modules might be "Camera Basics," "Composition," and "Post-Processing."
  • Chapters — A subdivision within a module. Chapters break a module into smaller, more focused groups of lessons. For example, under the "Camera Basics" module, you might have chapters like "Understanding Exposure," "Choosing Lenses," and "Shooting Modes."

The hierarchy works like this: Course > Module > Chapter > Lesson. You don't have to use all levels—if your course is simple, you can skip modules and organize lessons directly into chapters, or skip chapters entirely and place lessons directly inside modules.

Tip: Use modules for broad topic areas and chapters for narrower sub-topics within each module. This two-tier structure keeps even large courses easy to navigate.

Adding Chapters to Your Course

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Courses in the left sidebar and select the course you want to organize.
  3. Open the Content tab.
  4. If you're adding a chapter inside a module, click on the module first to expand it.
  5. Click the Add Chapter button.
  6. Enter a name for your chapter—choose something descriptive that tells students what they'll learn in this section.
  7. Click Save to create the chapter.

The new chapter appears in your course structure, ready for you to add lessons to it.

Adding Lessons to a Chapter

  1. Click on the chapter to expand it.
  2. Click Add Lesson inside the chapter.
  3. Enter the lesson name and configure the lesson type (Text, Video, or Audio).
  4. Click Save.

You can also move existing lessons into a chapter by dragging and dropping them from another location in the course structure.

Reordering Chapters and Lessons

Thrive Apprentice uses a drag-and-drop interface to make reordering simple:

  1. Open the Content tab of your course.
  2. Hover over the chapter or lesson you want to move until you see the drag handle (the icon with horizontal lines).
  3. Click and hold the drag handle, then drag the item to its new position.
  4. Release to drop it in place.

You can reorder chapters within a module, move lessons between chapters, or rearrange lessons within the same chapter—all with drag and drop.

Note: The order you set here is the order students see when they navigate the course. Make sure the sequence follows a logical learning progression.

Renaming and Deleting Chapters

To rename a chapter:

  1. Hover over the chapter in the Content tab.
  2. Click the Edit icon (pencil) that appears.
  3. Update the chapter name.
  4. Click Save.

To delete a chapter:

  1. Hover over the chapter you want to remove.
  2. Click the Delete icon (trash can).
  3. Confirm the deletion when prompted.

Important: Deleting a chapter also removes all lessons inside it. If you want to keep the lessons, move them to another chapter or module before deleting.

Best Practices for Course Structure

A well-organized course keeps students engaged and reduces dropout rates. Here are some guidelines:

  • Keep chapters focused. Each chapter should cover one specific sub-topic. If a chapter has more than 8-10 lessons, consider splitting it into two.
  • Use descriptive names. Chapter titles should clearly communicate what the student will learn. "Setting Up Your Workspace" is more helpful than "Chapter 1."
  • Follow a logical progression. Arrange chapters so each one builds on the previous. Start with foundational concepts and work toward advanced material.
  • Be consistent. Maintain a similar structure across modules—if one module uses chapters, the others should too. Consistency helps students know what to expect.
  • Don't over-nest. While the Course > Module > Chapter > Lesson hierarchy is powerful, not every course needs all four levels. Use only what makes sense for your content's complexity.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully learned how to create chapters, add lessons to them, reorder your course content, and apply best practices for course organization. A clear structure makes your course more professional and helps students stay on track from start to finish.

t: How to Set Up Menus for Your Courses and Lessons
c:
In this article, you'll learn how to create a dedicated WordPress navigation menu for your Thrive Apprentice courses and lessons—so students can easily browse your learning content without cluttering your main site menu.

Why Use a Separate Menu for Courses?

Your main website navigation is designed for general visitors. A dedicated course menu lets you tailor the navigation experience specifically for students, highlighting courses, lessons, and resources that matter most to learners.

Creating a New Menu

  1. In your WordPress dashboard, go to Appearance > Menus.
  2. Click the create a new menu link near the top of the page.
  3. Enter a descriptive name for your menu (e.g., "Course Navigation" or "Student Menu").
  4. Click Create Menu to save it.

Tip: Always create a new menu rather than modifying your existing site menu. This keeps your course navigation separate and easier to manage.

Adding Course and Lesson Links

With your new menu created, you can now add items to it.

  1. On the left side of the Menus screen, locate the Pages, Custom Links, or Categories panels.
  2. To add your main courses page, check the box next to it under Pages and click Add to Menu.
  3. To add individual course or lesson links, use the Custom Links panel—enter the URL and link text, then click Add to Menu.
  4. Drag and drop menu items to reorder them or create dropdown sub-menus by nesting items.
  5. Click Save Menu when you're finished.

Note: If you have many courses, consider organizing them into dropdown groups—for example, a top-level "Courses" item with individual courses nested beneath it.

Assigning the Menu to Your Course Pages

After building your menu, you need to tell WordPress where to display it.

  1. Scroll down to the Menu Settings section at the bottom of the Menus page.
  2. Under Display location, check the box that corresponds to the menu position you want (this depends on your theme—common options include Primary Menu, Header Menu, or Secondary Menu).
  3. Click Save Menu.

If your theme supports it, you can assign this menu exclusively to your Thrive Apprentice course and lesson pages using a plugin like Conditional Menus or through Thrive Theme Builder navigation settings.

Best Practices

  • Keep your course menu focused—include only items relevant to students.
  • Use clear, descriptive labels so learners know exactly where each link leads.
  • Add a link back to your main site or homepage so students can navigate away from the course area easily.
  • Test your menu on both desktop and mobile devices to ensure it displays correctly.

Important: If you update your course structure—adding or removing courses—remember to update your menu to match.

That's it! You've successfully created a dedicated navigation menu for your Thrive Apprentice courses and lessons, giving your students a clean and focused browsing experience.

t: How to Set Up Thrive Apprentice Email Templates
c:
In this article, you'll learn how to customize the email templates that Thrive Apprentice sends to your students—including welcome emails, course access notifications, and more—so every message matches your brand and delivers the right information.

What Are Email Templates?

Thrive Apprentice automatically sends emails to students at key moments—such as when they enroll in a course, receive access to new content, or complete a course. Email templates let you control the content, design, and personalization of these automated messages.

Accessing Email Templates

  1. Go to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Settings in the left sidebar.
  3. Select Email Templates from the settings menu.

Important: Before you can customize templates, you must configure an email delivery service provider. If you haven't done this yet, Thrive Apprentice will prompt you to select one when you first open the Email Templates settings.

Available Email Templates

Thrive Apprentice includes templates for the most common student communications:

  • Welcome Email — Sent when a student first registers or gains access to your platform.
  • Course Access Email — Sent when a student is granted access to a specific course.
  • Course Completion Email — Sent when a student finishes all lessons in a course.
  • Certificate Email — Sent when a student earns a certificate upon course completion.

Note: The exact templates available may vary depending on your Thrive Apprentice configuration and connected integrations.

Customizing an Email Template

  1. On the Email Templates screen, click the template you want to edit.
  2. Modify the Subject Line to reflect your branding or messaging.
  3. Edit the Email Body using the built-in editor. You can adjust text, formatting, and layout.
  4. Insert Dynamic Tags (also called merge fields) to personalize each email automatically.
  5. Click Save when you're finished.

Using Dynamic Tags for Personalization

Dynamic tags let you insert student-specific or course-specific information into your emails. Common tags include:

  • Student Name — Inserts the student's first name or full name.
  • Course Name — Inserts the name of the relevant course.
  • Course URL — Adds a direct link to the course.
  • Site Name — Inserts your website's name.

To insert a dynamic tag, place your cursor in the email body where you want the tag to appear and select the tag from the available options in the editor toolbar.

Testing Your Emails

Always test your emails before they go live to make sure everything looks correct.

  1. After editing a template, click the Send Test Email button.
  2. Enter an email address where you'd like to receive the test.
  3. Check your inbox for the test email and review the content, formatting, and dynamic tag output.
  4. Make any necessary adjustments and save again.

Tip: Send test emails to multiple email clients (Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail) to verify that your formatting renders correctly across platforms.

That's it! You've successfully configured and customized your Thrive Apprentice email templates, ensuring your students receive polished, personalized communications at every stage of their learning journey.
